Publishes every observable value to an admitted bounded stream. Result serialization and retention failures remain visible delivery outcomes; they do not rewrite a successful side effect as a command failure. Once the stream overflows or fails, the execution is stopped: disposing its subscription cancels the command instead of producing into a stream that can no longer accept values.

summary: Runs a ReactiveUI command from hand-written code the way a generated Bridge call runs it.
Executes
with

and completes when the execution completes, after zero or more values, as a generated Bridge call of a command without a result does. A command that produces no value completes normally; the values are not returned.

p: Use it in hand-written code that runs a command on behalf of a Bridge call or inside a model turn, such as a wrapper command that a Bridge presents and that runs a native command whose input has no wire form, when the code handles the command's failure itself, runs outside any Bridge call, or needs completion without a value. A failure of the execution is rethrown unchanged, and Runic counts it as received by this call: it is never logged as

(Views event 1042), whether the caller lets it propagate, wraps it or handles it, inside or outside a Bridge call. Failures of other executions of the command that arrive while this one runs are held until it ends and are logged then, as during a Bridge call.
The execution's notifications follow the model turn that started it, as for a bridged execution. Cancelling
disposes the execution, which cancels a token-taking
body, and the returned task is cancelled. A token that is already cancelled does not start it.

is enough inside a Bridge call when the exception propagates or is wrapped: the Bridge call receives it. The Views.ReactiveUI guide's "Which call to use" section compares them.
